_comment: What the public site shows. Edit this file, then run build/refresh-prod.sh
(or refresh-demo.sh). No code change and no rebuild of the backend.
Every value here has been something we changed our minds about at least
once. That is the point: these are decisions, not constants, and they
belong somewhere a maintainer can reach without a diff.
A deployment can override any of these in its local_settings.py with
DISPLAY_CONFIG = {...}; anything absent falls back to what is here, so a
key added later cannot break a deployment that has not heard of it.

_doc: Hovering a pin shows a two-second orbit rendered from the published
model, instead of a still photograph. false shows the 160px still.
Rendered by `manage.py backfill_turntables`; a site with no rendered
orbit falls back to the still whatever this says. Roughly a third of
the rendered ones show haze rather than a monument, which is a property
of those reconstructions rather than of the renderer -- review them at
a sample of them before turning this on for a
wider audience.
The 'Beta' chip beside the wordmark.
null means decide automatically: shown on the demo and on beta, hidden
on production. true or false overrides that everywhere. It was
unconditional once, which would have told every production visitor the
archive is provisional.
Which languages the switcher offers. The server still serves any of
them by URL, and an existing /hi/ link keeps working -- this controls
what is advertised, not what resolves.
Hindi is withheld: its translations are drafted but unreviewed.
How close two pins must be, in pixels, before the map merges them.
60 was MapLibre's default and clustered pins that did not visually
overlap, so a cluster appeared where two separate temples were plainly
distinguishable. 28 is about one pin's width: if they do not overlap,
they are not a cluster.
